q10_justification: Everything revolves around warfare - even primary school teachers carry weapons and society is built around fighting.
q11_justification: An absurdly militaristic civilization that punches potatoes as anger management doesn't map to traditional analogies.

q1_justification: The Krikkit robots unlock the Slo-Time envelope, releasing the imprisoned civilization and their armies. The Galaxy faces existential threat.
q2_justification: The Krikkit star system was sealed away from extensive galactic civilization; the Key components came from across many worlds.
q3_justification: The asteroid orbits the dust cloud around the Slo-Time envelope - at the extreme edge of the Galaxy, effectively unreachable.
q4_justification: The Wikkit Key's components include a cricket stump, a robot leg, and a profanity award - a radically alien symbolic system.
q5_justification: The characters communicate freely while observing; the robots chant 'Krikkit' in universal understanding.
q6_justification: Standing on an asteroid cliff requires the ship's field to prevent falling off; the environment needs technological support.
q7_justification: The Bistromath casually parks on an asteroid; standing on a cliff in vacuum is made routine by technology.
q8_justification: No galactic authority intervenes; the protagonists are helpless volunteers and the robots answer only to imprisoned Masters.
q9_justification: Zaphod's dramatic entrance only to be immediately knocked out, and the Wikkit Key made of absurd components, maintain comedic tone.
q10_justification: Krikkit military robots execute their mission while civilian protagonists watch helplessly; Zaphod attempts armed intervention.
q11_justification: Unlocking an imprisoned star system with a key made of a cricket stump and a profanity award is utterly unique.
q12_justification: An asteroid orbiting a dust cloud around a Slo-Time envelope, where space is 'pinched out of existence,' is fundamentally unlike Earth.
